newsitem.title: FRANCE: Fugitive French mayor to return from Argentina.
newsitem.headline: Fugitive French mayor to return from Argentina.

text.p: Fugitive French politician Jean- Michel Boucheron said in an interview published on Monday that he would not fight a French extradition request and would voluntarily return home from exile in Argentina to face justice.
Boucheron, 50, was sentenced in his absence in 1994 to four years in jail for taking bribes from utility contractors.
He was also fined a million francs ($175,000) and stripped of civil rights for five years.
A former Socialist parliamentarian and mayor of the southwestern city of Angouleme, he was convicted of influence-peddling, forging business documents and complicity to commit fraud.
He fled to Argentina where he opened a restaurant in Buenos Aires which, he told the newspaper "Charente Libre", had now gone out of business.
Boucheron said he was bankrupt and returning "because you cannot live with a sword of Damocles above your head forever".
